meaning: The remaining years of Peleg – the time after he fathered his son Reu
description: The number 209 appears in the Bible's genealogy in Genesis 11:19, where it states that Peleg lived 209 years after he fathered his son Reu, and during this time he had other sons and daughters. Peleg belongs to the line from Shem to Abraham, and his life thus forms part of the genealogical bridge between Noah's descendants and the patriarchs. Beyond this genealogical context, the number 209 has no widely recognized symbolic meaning in classical Jewish numerology or biblical theology. Although the gematria system can link Hebrew words to the numerical value 209, there is no consensus among scholars regarding a specific mystical role for this number.

footnotes.text: The name Peleg (פֶּלֶג) means 'division' or 'water stream'. According to Genesis 10:25, he was given this name because "in his days the earth was divided". Rabbinic tradition links this to the confusion of languages at Babel.

Peleg lived a total of 239 years (Gen 10:16–19), which was significantly shorter than that of his ancestors before him. Several commentators have viewed the gradual decline in lifespan after the flood as theologically significant.
